title: App Store Now Has AI Fraud Apps: Fake Screenshots Achieve 4.9 Stars, Developers Accuse Apple's Review Process Is Useless
excerpt: The developer of the Safari extension StopTheMadness, Jeff Johnson, published a blog post on August 13, pointing out obvious rating fraud on the Apple App Store
content_html:
The developer of the Safari extension StopTheMadness, Jeff Johnson, published a blog post on August 13, pointing out obvious rating fraud on the Apple App Store.

He used the paid Safari extension list on the US Mac App Store as an example. A program called TabControl climbed to the 12th position, but its promotional image seemed to be generated by AI, with a glaring "4.9 out of 5" rating that was clearly unreasonable. These apps, which use fake screenshots to "package" their reputation, are exploiting Apple's review blind spots to gain users' trust and downloads.

Johnson pointed out that using screenshots to show false ratings has become a common tactic for scam apps on the App Store. Some of these apps' screenshots have "obviously absurd" promotional content, yet they still passed Apple's review process and were approved for listing. He believes that when reviewing apps submitted to the App Store, Apple should include screenshots and rating displays in the review scope, rather than just focusing on functional descriptions and code compliance.

Safari Extension Permissions Pose Privacy Risks

More concerning is the identity of TabControl—it is a Safari browser extension, which can theoretically access users' web content, browsing behavior, and related system permissions. Once such fraudulent extensions are installed, users' privacy and security face real threats, which is fundamentally different from ordinary entertainment apps that inflate ratings. Johnson therefore emphasized that users should not trust any app that relies on deception to sell.

This incident once again reveals the long-standing issue of app store governance: with the prevalence of AI-generated content, the threshold for forging high-quality screenshots and fabricating reviews has been significantly lowered.

Apple has always promoted "strict review" as the core selling point of the App Store. However, when fake materials generated by AI can easily bypass the review, the credibility of this promise is inevitably questioned. For ordinary users, being more vigilant before downloading and paying less attention to "seller's photos" might be the most practical defense at the moment—and when platforms truly prioritize screenshot reviews will determine the final outcome of this cat-and-mouse game.

content_html_zh:
Safari 扩展 StopTheMadness 的开发者 Jeff Johnson 于 8 月 13 日发表博文，指出苹果应用商店存在明显的评级欺诈行为。

他以美国 Mac App Store 上的付费 Safari 扩展列表为例。 一款名为 TabControl 的程序攀升至第 12 位，但其宣传形象似乎是由 AI 生成的，其评分为“4.9 分（满分 5 分）”，显然不合理。 这些应用程序利用虚假屏幕截图来“包装”自己的声誉，正在利用苹果的审核盲点来获取用户的信任和下载。

约翰逊指出，使用屏幕截图显示虚假评级已成为 App Store 上诈骗应用程序的常见策略。 其中一些应用程序的屏幕截图具有“明显荒谬”的宣传内容，但它们仍然通过了苹果的审核程序并被批准上市。 他认为，苹果在审核提交到App Store的应用程序时，应该将截图和评级显示纳入审核范围，而不是仅仅关注功能描述和代码合规性。

Safari 扩展权限带来隐私风险

更值得关注的是TabControl的身份——它是一个Safari浏览器扩展，理论上可以访问用户的网页内容、浏览行为以及相关的系统权限。 一旦安装了此类欺诈性扩展程序，用户的隐私和安全将面临真正的威胁，这与普通娱乐应用程序夸大评级的行为有着本质的区别。 约翰逊因此强调，用户不应相信任何依靠欺骗来销售的应用程序。

这一事件再次暴露了应用商店治理长期存在的问题：随着人工智能生成内容的盛行，伪造高质量截图和捏造评论的门槛已大大降低。

苹果一直将“严格审核”作为App Store的核心卖点。 然而，当人工智能生成的虚假材料可以轻松绕过审查时，这一承诺的可信度不可避免地受到质疑。 对于普通用户来说，在下载前提高警惕，少关注“卖家照片”可能是目前最实际的防御——而当平台真正优先考虑截图审核时，将决定这场猫鼠游戏的最终结果。
